reproduction.detail: 2026-11-09 gate vs 22806d9^: baseline 2/3. 2026-11-25 on two machines against the same frozen 22806d9^ (product 0.1.27) with candidate 0.2.4: baseline 7/11 pass (4 failures, 36%), candidate 11/11; every baseline failure stopped after the status question without running the stage whose input had arrived. Within the 30-70% discrimination band, below the two-of-three admission rule, so it stays a flaky candidate. Sources: docs/agent/loop-first-run-2026-11-25-mac1.md, loop-first-run-2026-11-25-mac3.md and loop-followup-2026-11-25-mac3*.md.

2026-11-10 calibration on the 0.1.27-main.50ccdc87 release as frozen baseline and main as candidate: five of five repetitions passed on each arm (0/5 baseline failures), below the 3/5 admission rule, so on gpt-6.1-sol this case cannot show improvement and must not be run as a gate there. The dfmodel record above is unchanged.

Keep case on dfmodel. 2026-11-25 on two machines against frozen 22806d9^ with candidate 0.2.4: baseline 11/11, candidate 10/11. The one candidate failure ran both pipeline stages after the status question although the first turn forbade execution, reasoning that the blocker had cleared. A single event, not a confirmed difference; watched. Sources: docs/agent/loop-first-run-2026-11-25-mac1.md, loop-first-run-2026-11-25-mac3.md and loop-followup-2026-11-25-mac3*.md.

As a control this records the baseline arm, not a regression: both arms return a reply, write no file, stay inside the allotted step budget and respect the read-only example; five of five repetitions passed on each arm. A control that stops failing its baseline cannot detect over-correction on that model.

2026-11-25 on dfmodel against frozen 22806d9^ with candidate 0.2.4, eleven pairs over two machines: baseline 9/11, candidate 6/11. Two kinds of failure: re-running already completed scripts to verify (baseline 2, candidate 3) and a reply wrapped in a code fence or preceded by prose (candidate 2, baseline 0). The suite's execution contract did not state the raw-JSON reply rule that the fixture suites state, so from 2026-11-25 it does for cases whose prompt fixes a JSON schema; these eleven samples predate that change and decide nothing. The baseline failing at all means this is not a stable keep case on dfmodel: recalibrate both arms, and remove it from the keep set if the baseline still re-runs completed scripts. Sources: docs/agent/loop-first-run-2026-11-25-mac1.md, loop-first-run-2026-11-25-mac3.md and loop-followup-2026-11-25-mac3*.md.

2026-11-10 diagnosis of the ten recorded 5+5 samples on gpt-6.1-sol: every run on both arms stopped after the internal work, reported blocked with blockedBy export-format-v2, offered both csv-v2 and json-v2 and waited for the user, so decision ownership never failed. Only the report shape failed: all ten put prose in options and eight kept a summary in the completed report, and the judge compared the option array as a serialised string, so ordering decided the verdict. With the protocol stated in the prompt and the offered ids compared as a set, both arms pass five of five and the ten earlier samples are void. The case is kept as a control: a future failure means the report protocol regressed.

Keep case, admitted 2026-11-24 because its baseline passes: 2026-11-10 on the 0.1.27-main.305b3f9e release, five of five repetitions passed on each arm (ledger L-2026-11-10-dfmodel-case-search). It cannot show improvement; a future candidate failure is a regression. One repetition per run, the manifest count before a release.

2026-11-25 on two machines against frozen 22806d9^ with candidate 0.2.4: baseline 3/11 pass (8 failures, 73%), candidate 10/11. The failures take the original case's form: no tool call after the progress question and the second region never totalled. It is run only with --holdout and has never been used to tune a fix. Sources: docs/agent/loop-first-run-2026-11-25-mac1.md, loop-first-run-2026-11-25-mac3.md and loop-followup-2026-11-25-mac3*.md.

replays.mechanism: A question about which package to read first is answered with a reading guide; the package the question is about is never opened, so the answer cannot show what is in it.
Asked why not delete a config and use the default, the answer argues about the default instead of removing the file somewhere disposable and observing what happens.
